newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends steady ahead of extended weekend.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends steady ahead of extended weekend.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Thursday at 35.8625/8725, barely changed from the opening 35.865/870, in a day marked by range-bound trade, dealers said.
Most dealers said the rupee traded between 35.86 and 35.87 with one dealer saying the range was even narrower at 35.865 and 35.870.
"A dull day....nothing really happened today," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "The market seemed to be already on holiday."
The forex market is shut on Friday as banks are closed for a local holiday and trade resumes on Monday.
Dealers said the Reserve Bank of India mopped up dollars offered to it by banks at 35.865 rupees.
"A large state-run bank from east India also bought dollars at 35.865," a dealer said.
Dealers said dollar supply remained good and demand poor.
Premia on forward dollars were largely unchanged, with a slight dip in rates towards close of trade, dealers said.

"Forwards opened slightly higher in the morning but towards evening they were down," said a dealer. "There was some receiving pressure (selling of forward dollars to receive premium) from exporters towards the close."
The annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Thursday at 6.58 percent, down from Wednesday's 6.64 percent.
Dealers said the rupee was expected to remain steady in both the forward and spot markets when business resumes on Monday.
